question: What does the school logo mean?
answer:
The school logo is packed with symbols that tell the story of Philippine Advent College, Inc.:

• Bible – shown wide‑open in the center, representing the foundation of Christian education.
• Torch (light) – placed behind the Bible, it illuminates the book and the institution, showing that God is the true source of all wisdom and that the college’s influence extends to its stakeholders.
• 1975 – the year the college was founded and began spreading its light to the community.
• Blue background – symbolizes royalty.
• Red lettering – stands for passion, love, and the power to carry the light.
• White center – the background behind the Bible, representing the purity of the college’s mission.

Together, these elements convey a purpose‑driven, Christ‑centered identity that guides students and staff.

(More detail is on page 10.)

question: Something about 1975?
answer:
1975 – The founding year of Philippine Advent College (PAC)

• Establishment: 1975 is the year PAC was officially founded. The logo even highlights “1975” to mark when the institution began its mission and influence in the community.

• Original name: At its start it was called Hillside View Elementary School (HVES). In the same year it transitioned from an elementary school to an academy and later grew into a college.

• Founders: The school was founded by former Mayor Mariano J.S. Macias and Margie C. Macias, together with their children, who played a key role in setting up the institution.

• Community support: The launch was strongly backed by the local Seventh‑day Adventist church and elders from nearby towns, forming the first governing incorporators.

So, 1975 marks the birth and early transformation of PAC from a small elementary school into the college it is today.

(More detail is on page 6 and page 10.)

question: What happens if you get 20 or more demerits?
answer:
If you reach 20 or more demerits you are put on probation right away (as long as this happens less than one month before the term ends).

What probation means

• You cannot hold any office or responsibility for the rest of the midterm or the semester‑end period.
• The Student Disciplinary Committee reviews your probation status.
• The home dean and academic chairpersons can recommend that probation be maintained or lifted.

Limits on probation

• No student may stay on probation for more than one semester.
• If probation is not lifted by the end of that semester, you are denied admission for the next term.

Other standard measures that accompany any demerits

• You must write an explanation of the offense and acknowledge it.
• Parents are notified, and the guidance counselor and faculty adviser help with counseling.
• Community service or a fine (up to P1,500.00) may be imposed, depending on the severity.

question: What's the dress code for students?
answer:
General student dress code

• Dress modestly and neatly in harmony with PAC standards.
• Leave all jewelry (rings, bracelets, necklaces) at home except a wedding ring.
• No slippers, short/city shorts, backless or crop tops are allowed on campus.
• No indecent or obscene words/prints on T‑shirts.
• No tight‑fitting pants or clothing with suggestive patches/prints.

Ladies

• Jeans and square pants are not allowed during religious or formal services/programs.
• Dresses must cover the knee when sitting or standing; any slit must be at least 3 inches below the knee.
• Avoid dresses that are transparent without proper lining, sleeveless, or snug‑fitting skirts.

Men

• Wear a suit, white or light‑colored shirt with tie, barong Tagalog, or long‑sleeve shirt with necktie for religious and formal services/programs.
• Same restrictions on T‑shirts, tight‑fitting pants, and indecent prints apply.

question: What's the Safe Spaces Act and its RA number?
answer:
Safe Spaces Act – a law that protects students and faculty from gender‑based sexual harassment and promotes a safe, respectful, and inclusive learning environment.

RA number: Republic Act 11313 (Safe Spaces Act of 2019)

(More detail is on page 22.)

question: What about RA 11313?
answer:
RA 11313 – the Safe Spaces Act of 2019

• It is the law that guides Philippine Advent College’s policy on Gender‑Based Sexual Harassment (GBSH).

• The Act requires the school to create a safe, respectful, and inclusive learning environment for all students and faculty.

• Under RA 11313, GBSH includes any unwelcome sexual behavior—verbal, physical, or online—based on sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. Examples listed are:
- Catcalling, sexist remarks, intrusive comments or looks
- Unwanted touching or physical contact
- Stalking
- Sharing or posting sexual content without consent (including nude images)
- Cyber‑harassment, sexual advances online, or inappropriate messages
- Homophobic or transphobic slurs

• Scope of protection (as required by the Act) covers:
- All school premises and facilities
- Online platforms used for classes or communication
- School activities, whether on‑ or off‑campus
- Public spaces within the educational environment

• To comply with RA 11313, the college has set up a Gender‑Based Harassment Committee (GBHC) that:
- Manages complaints and investigations
- Provides support to survivors
